About

The analysis is only finished when someone can act on it.

I'm finishing a bachelor's in Artificial Intelligence Engineering at Egyptian Russian University, graduating in 2026 with a Very Good standing. Somewhere between the coursework and the training programs I found the work I actually want to do: taking a dataset nobody has cleaned yet, understanding what it's hiding, and handing back something a manager can make a decision from before lunch.

Day to day that means Power BI, SQL, Excel and Python — data modelling, DAX measures, exploratory analysis, dashboards designed around the questions people ask rather than the columns the data happens to have. When a dashboard isn't enough, I train a model: classification, prediction, sentiment analysis, image recognition.

Five training programs shaped how I work — Huawei's HCIA-AI and HCIA-Big Data tracks, 72 hours at ITI, a five-month Data Science intensive with Microsoft Student Club at EELU, and a Power BI-focused analysis track with GDG on Campus. I'm early in my career and I won't pretend otherwise. What I bring is fundamentals that hold up, real dashboards I can walk you through screenshot by screenshot, and the habit of asking what decision the output is meant to support before I open a single file.
